title: Linking your ideas
topic: simple connectors: y/e, o/u, pero, porque, cuando, también, además, entonces
why: After estar + gerund and ir a + infinitive, this lesson teaches you to link your sentences: y/e, o/u, pero/sino, porque, cuando and storytelling connectors. You move from isolated sentences to a short, smooth account of your routine, which prepares you for the big review conversation.

Y, o, pero: little words that change shape

Y (and), o (or) and pero (but) are used just like in English. But y and o change shape in front of certain sounds, to avoid two identical vowels running together.

Y becomes e before the “ee” sound

In front of a word that starts with i- or hi- (the h is silent), y becomes e:

SpanishEnglish
padre e hijofather and son
español e inglésSpanish and English
Lucía e InésLucía and Inés
geografía e historiageography and history

Exception: in front of hie-, pronounced like “yeh”, you keep y: agua y hielo (water and ice).

O becomes u before the “o” sound

In front of a word that starts with o- or ho-, o becomes u: siete u ocho, uno u otro, mujer u hombre.

Pero or sino?

English has only one “but”. Spanish has two:

  • pero adds a contrasting idea: Es caro, pero me gusta (it's expensive, but I like it).
  • sino corrects something after a negative: “not this, but that”. No es rojo sino verde. No vivo en Madrid sino en Toledo.
No hablo italiano sino francés, pero entiendo un poco el italiano.I don't speak Italian but French, but I understand a bit of Italian.

The test: if you can say “not… but rather…”, it's sino. Otherwise, it's pero. Don't confuse sino (one word) with si no (if… not).

", "

Porque, por qué, cuando

Porque and ¿por qué?

You've already seen them: ¿por qué?, two words with an accent, asks the question (why?); porque, one word with no accent, gives the answer (because).

¿Por qué estudias español? — Porque mi pareja es de Murcia.Why are you studying Spanish? — Because my partner is from Murcia.

Cuando + present: habits

Cuando (when), with no accent, links two habitual actions. As in English, you use the present on both sides.

SpanishEnglish
Cuando llego a casa, me ducho.When I get home, I take a shower.
Cuando hace calor, vamos a la playa.When it's hot, we go to the beach.
Leo cuando estoy en el metro.I read when I'm on the subway.

In a question, ¿cuándo? takes an accent: ¿Cuándo comes? In a sentence that links two ideas, no accent: Como cuando tengo hambre.

Careful: cuando + present is for habits. For a future moment (“when I'm in Madrid next month”), English still uses the present, but Spanish uses another mood, the subjunctive, which you'll see later. For now, stick to habits.

", "

Telling your day smoothly

To link the steps of a routine, here are the most useful connectors.

SpanishEnglish
primerofirst
luegothen, next
despuésafter that, afterwards
más tardelater
entoncesso, then
ademásbesides, what's more
tambiénalso, too
al finalin the end, finally

Después de, antes de + infinitive

In front of a noun or an infinitive, después and antes take de: después de comer (after eating), antes de dormir (before sleeping), después del trabajo (after work). English uses the “-ing” form after “after” and “before”; Spanish always uses the infinitive after a preposition, never the gerund.

Primero me levanto y desayuno. Luego voy a la oficina en metro. Después de comer, tomo un café con mis compañeros. Cuando salgo del trabajo, voy al gimnasio o paseo un poco. Al final, ceno y leo antes de dormir.First I get up and have breakfast. Then I go to the office by subway. After lunch, I have a coffee with my coworkers. When I leave work, I go to the gym or go for a little walk. Finally, I have dinner and read before going to sleep.

Además and después have a written accent. Además means “besides, what's more”: it adds an argument in the same direction. Entonces is also used to draw a conclusion, like “so”: Estoy cansado, entonces voy a dormir.
